meaning: MEAN_WINDOW_S = 10 declares that the data were averaged over a 10 s window on the 1 Hz grid, matching what scripts/prep_jugular_data.py applied. It is the smoothing width the fit scores against and the width quoted in panel titles.

could_move.what: Scored residuals in the m5 fit, since the same window constant is used where the fit compares model to data
A second use inside the m5 fit path, so a change would move both sites together
Data panel curves and the window quoted in their titles
Second panel site, same risk of title/curve disagreement
The m1 copy of this constant; if only one is edited, m1 and m5 are scored on different smoothing
Patient decks that overlay m5 against recordings
Model-vs-model comparison decks, where an asymmetric edit would bias the comparison
Numbers written into the fitting write-up

expectation: Unknown in size. Direction: a wider window smooths peaks and troughs further, so amplitude-sensitive residuals shrink and fitted amplitudes can drift; a narrower one does the reverse. Whether the preprocessing script still applies 10 s cannot be told from this context.

check.why: Re-scores the stored m5 fit against the data grid without re-fitting, so any mismatch between this window and the preprocessing shows up in the residuals.
